evals.prompt: Classify a bounded row containing a human-interest story about a singer winning a recording session. Use title, URL slug, and description first; do not open the article.
evals.expected_output: The record is routed to noncrime with empty Good Categories and Bad Categories, evidence explaining the human-interest basis, and no article fetch.
assertions: No article fetch is performed when metadata clearly establishes noncrime
The result has no Good Category
The result preserves an evidence phrase and confidence

evals.prompt: Classify a US article stating that a toddler died after accessing an unattended firearm and the uncle was charged with unlawful firearm possession. Assign all supported categories and use readable subcategory names.
evals.expected_output: The result includes both unlawful firearm possession and child dangerous-exposure context in Good Categories, with one line per primary category and no machine codes; Bad Categories are evaluated separately.
assertions: Both weapon and Child Neglect, Endangerment & Child Abuse categories are assigned when adult responsibility and dangerous exposure are supported
The category rendering uses human-readable names rather than codes
Each distinct primary category is on its own line

evals.prompt: Classify a federal school-funds fraud article involving wire fraud, kickbacks, an institutional setting, and arrests. Do not run the final client selection policy unless explicitly requested.
evals.expected_output: The result retains all supported category-stage labels and leaves selection_outcome as not_run; it does not research or decide the future federal/financial policy outcome.
assertions: Good Categories and any Bad Categories are not erased because the case may later be excluded
The final policy outcome remains not_run
Missing optional policy facts do not trigger deeper research

evals.prompt: Classify a child-pornography possession or attempted-purchase article under the updated primary taxonomy.
evals.expected_output: The result uses the Bad Category Sexual Crimes / Exploitation when supported and does not use Human Trafficking, Forced Labor & Exploitation without force, coercion, control, child commercial exploitation, or an explicit trafficking allegation.
assertions: Sexual Crimes / Exploitation is rendered as a Bad Category
Human Trafficking is rejected without trafficking or commercial-exploitation evidence
No neighboring Good Category is invented merely to fill the Good cell

evals.prompt: Classify a clearly described crime whose title, description, and URL slug contain no foreign-location signal and no category ambiguity.
evals.expected_output: The record uses the U.S. routing default, does not fetch solely to verify country, and receives no Excluded: Out of US label.
assertions: No geography-only fetch occurs without a credible foreign hint
Location assessment may be assumed_us
Out of US is not guessed

evals.prompt: Classify a crime record whose metadata credibly suggests that the incident occurred outside the United States but is not conclusive.
evals.expected_output: The original article may be fetched to resolve the foreign-location hint; Excluded: Out of US is assigned only if incident location is affirmatively confirmed.
assertions: Publisher location and domain are not treated as incident location
A credible foreign hint can trigger targeted original-article review
Unresolved geography becomes review evidence rather than a guessed bad category

evals.prompt: Classify three concise records: coerced forced labor, noncoercive paid human smuggling, and voluntary adult prostitution.
evals.expected_output: Forced labor receives the Good Human Trafficking parent; noncoercive human smuggling receives Bad Excluded; voluntary adult prostitution receives Bad Prostitution / Commercial Sex.
assertions: Force, coercion, control, exploitation, or child commercial exploitation is required for the Good trafficking parent
Noncoercive human smuggling is not labeled Good trafficking
Voluntary adult commercial sex is not labeled trafficking

evals.prompt: Classify an organized cross-border operation concealing illegal firearms and stolen goods in cargo.
evals.expected_output: The record receives Organized Contraband Smuggling plus every independently supported Weapons and Theft category.
assertions: Organized Contraband Smuggling requires operation-level movement or concealment evidence
The specific substantive offense categories are additive
Ordinary local possession would not qualify for the smuggling parent

evals.prompt: Classify a crime with a supported Good parent and Bad parent, but no exact maintained subcategory on either side.
evals.expected_output: Both supported parents remain visible, both subcategory gaps appear in column P with Good/Bad prefixes and evidence notes, and needs_review is true.
assertions: A supported parent does not require a forced subcategory
Good and bad unmapped candidates are both preserved
Any unmapped candidate requires manual review

evals.prompt: Classify a story involving both a human assault and material deliberate harm to an animal.
evals.expected_output: The result keeps the supported human-directed Good Category and also assigns Bad Animal-Related Stories with the supported animal subcategory.
assertions: Animal-Related Stories applies whenever animal or wildlife involvement is material
The animal bad category does not suppress supported human-directed categories
An incidental animal mention alone does not trigger the category

evals.prompt: Render two classified rows: one successfully fetched article and one article fetch that failed and needs manual intervention.
evals.expected_output: Column N is Yes for both attempted article paths, the failed row remains needs_review with diagnostics, evidence is in O, unmapped candidates are in P, and confidence remains only in local records.
assertions: Fetched, fetch_failed, and infrastructure_error statuses render Yes in column N
A failed attempt requires needs_review and retained diagnostics
The six Sheet values are K:P and contain no confidence value
